construct: SERPING1-related C1-inhibitor deficiency or dysfunction permits excessive kallikrein/contact-system activity and overproduction of bradykinin, causing episodic nonurticarial edema of skin, bowel, and upper airway.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Recurrent nonpruritic nonurticarial edema and abdominal attacks, affected relatives, low C4, and reduced C1-inhibitor function identify hereditary angioedema from C1-inhibitor deficiency/dysfunction and bradykinin excess.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Acquired C1-inhibitor deficiency is the strongest mechanistic alternative because it shares complement abnormalities, but the young age and multigenerational family history strongly favor hereditary disease. IgE/anaphylaxis and chronic urticaria are histamine-associated, while ACE-inhibitor angioedema requires drug exposure.
